concerns.text: Tasks T000-FIX-SPEC and T000-FIX-PLAN instruct the implementer to edit upstream artifacts (spec.md, plan.md) directly. This violates Constitution Principle V (Versioning Discipline) which requires artifact changes to be tracked via content hashes and state updates, not ad-hed edits in a task list. A task cannot 'fix' a spec without a formal versioning event.

Tasks T075-T085 implement 'Review-Driven Operationalization' metrics (falsification, metabolic cost, irreducibility, etc.) that are not defined in spec.md FR-001 through FR-007. This constitutes unapproved scope creep and violates the strict boundary on measurable outcomes defined in the spec and Constitution Principle VII.

Task T019a-TIE implements a fallback tie-breaking rule ('fall back to highest average confidence score') if the first path is invalid. This contradicts spec.md Edge Cases which explicitly mandate a deterministic rule ('prefer the first generated path') with no fallback, creating a semantic weakening of the acceptance criteria.

Task T012-IMPL defines a training proxy using N=3 samples for majority vote. While the note claims this is distinct from FR-003's N=10 for evaluation, the spec does not explicitly authorize a different N for training. This introduces a silent constitution drift regarding the 'self-consistency proxy' definition without explicit spec approval.

Task T004a-FETCH saves raw stream data but lacks explicit instructions to calculate and record the checksum in state/...yaml or data/manifest.json immediately upon write. This violates Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) which requires datasets to be checksummed and recorded.
